cards.text: Paul the apostle is writing to the believers. He calls himself a prisoner in the Lord, and he's STILL the one giving the pep talk. Friend, in my junk drawer years, the most I ever managed was counting dust.

cards.question: Paul writes as a prisoner in the Lord. What does he urge the believers to do?
Paul starts listing what a worthy walk looks like. Which of these is on his list?

cards.text: Next up is bearing with one another in love. That's for the coworker who hits reply-all on EVERY email, friend, and yes, you bear with them IN LOVE.

cards.question: Paul also puts patience on his list for a worthy walk.

cards.text: And Paul says don't just coast on this. Put in some diligence, because there's something here worth guarding.

cards.question: Paul tells the believers to put in diligence. What are they supposed to preserve?
Paul says the unity of the Spirit is held together through strict rules.

cards.text: Not rules, friend. The bond of peace. Then Paul starts a list, and every item on it begins with the same little word.

cards.question: Every item on Paul's list of what believers share begins with the word ___.

cards.text: One body, one Spirit, one hope, one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all. SEVEN "ones" in three verses, friend, and I ran out of mustache to count on.

cards.question: Paul calls Him the one God and Father of all. Where does Paul say this God is?

answers.text: Over all and through all and in all
Above all and far from all

cards.question: Paul says each church gets its own Lord and its own faith.

cards.text: Now Paul turns a corner. He's talked about what all believers share, and now he talks about what each one gets.

cards.question: Paul says that to each one of us, ___ has been given according to the measure of the gift of Christ.

cards.text: Paul backs it up with Scripture: “When He ascended on high, He led captives away, and gave gifts to men.”
Then Paul asks a question. If He ascended, doesn't that mean He also descended to the lower parts of the earth?

cards.question: Paul says the One who came down is the same One who went up above all the heavens. Why did He go up?
The Scripture said He gave gifts to men. Then Paul names some of those gifts, and they're people. Which of these are on the list?

cards.text: Evangelists too, and pastors and teachers, and not one of them is listed as the guy who does everything. Trust me, friend, I tried being that guy in my bakery, and that's EXACTLY why I invited you.

cards.question: Why did He give apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors and teachers?

answers.text: To equip the saints for ministry
To gather offerings for the poor

cards.question: Paul says these apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors and teachers are given to build up the body of Christ.
Paul says building up the body of Christ stops once the church has enough leaders.

cards.text: It keeps going until we all reach unity in the faith and in the knowledge of the Son of God. We mature to the full measure of the stature of Christ.

cards.question: Paul says that once believers mature, they'll no longer be ___.

cards.text: Infants get tossed about by the waves and carried around by every wind of teaching. It's like the friend who believes whatever video he watched LAST, then changes his mind every time he scrolls.

cards.question: Paul says every wind of teaching blowing around is harmless.

cards.text: Paul also warns about the clever cunning of men in their deceitful scheming. But Paul has a better way to talk.

cards.question: Instead of being tossed about like infants, how does Paul say believers should speak?
Speaking the truth in love, we grow up into Christ Himself, who is the ___ of the body.

cards.text: From Him the whole body is fitted and held together by every supporting ligament. Ligaments, friend, the parts nobody thanks until they pull one reaching for the snooze button.

cards.question: Paul says the whole body grows and builds itself up. Through what?

answers.text: The work of each individual part
The work of its leaders only
The strength of its biggest parts

cards.question: The whole body grows and builds itself up in ___.

findings.problem: Ephesians 4:1 opens mid-thought with 'then', pointing back to chapters 1–3. The opening card never gives that context.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The card names Paul the apostle as the writer, but that fact isn't in Ephesians 4:1-16. The card carries no reference for it, such as Ephesians 1:1.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The joke says the most Papa Dorin ever managed in the drawer was counting dust. His backstory says he welcomed, calmed and helped every newcomer there, which is exactly what Paul is doing here. The joke changes his story.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The card says 'Next up is bearing with one another in love,' but in Ephesians 4:2 patience comes before bearing with one another. Card 5 then asks about patience after the card has already moved past it.

rule.text: He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The card cites Ephesians 4:3-4, but it says every item on the list begins with the same word. That describes the whole list in Ephesians 4:4-6, so the citation should be Ephesians 4:3-6.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This story card lists 'one Lord, one faith,' which gives away card 13. Card 13 asks whether each church gets its own Lord and its own faith. Card 13 also steps back from verse 6 to verse 5.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'Over all and through all and in all' (8 words), is longer and more Bible-sounding than the wrong answers (5 words each), so it stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Above all and far from all' starts with 'above all,' which means almost the same as the right answer's 'over all.' A baker could argue it is partly right.

rule.text: A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Gently and seldom' is arguably true in this passage, since Ephesians 4:2 calls for gentleness. A baker could argue that speaking gently fits.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'The truth in love,' is a noun phrase. The wrong answers, 'Gently and seldom' and 'Boldly and loudly,' are adverb pairs. The right answer stands out as the only Bible-sounding one.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone.
